acceptance: Image runs rootless, has health checks, SBOM, signature, and no embedded secrets.
verifiedBy: node --test tests/oci/generate-oci-release.test.mjs (8/8 pass) and node --test tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs (5/5 pass), executed together -- see commands.log. node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-910 (the manifest command) was not run; per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md the manifest commands list runs once at the final phased book gate, not per task.
observed: Rootless: packaging/oci/Containerfile sets `USER 65532:65532` before ENTRYPOINT, asserted by tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs's `^USER 65532:65532$` regex match -- the process never runs as UID 0. Health checks: the Containerfile's HEALTHCHECK now invokes `membrane cli doctor paths`, a real, read-only, non-interactive CLI subcommand implemented in engine/crates/membrane/src/modes.rs (is_doctor_paths_invocation/run_doctor_paths) and covered by that crate's own tests, replacing a prior HEALTHCHECK that invoked `membrane health --headless`, a command that does not exist anywhere in engine/crates/membrane; tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs was updated to assert the real command literally. SBOM and signature: scripts/release/oci/generate-oci-release.mjs requires real, already-produced --sbom, --ed25519, and --cosign evidence files, independently recomputes each file's sha256, and hands the assembled candidate to the pre-existing scripts/release/verify-oci-release.mjs#verifyOciRelease -- which re-verifies every evidence file's path (repo-relative, no traversal, regular file, not a symlink) and hash before treating the release as 'ready'. tests/oci/generate-oci-release.test.mjs proves this end to end with real fixture files under a temp directory: a candidate with all evidence present validates and writes; a candidate missing any one evidence file fails closed with no write. No embedded secrets: tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs asserts the Containerfile contains no SECRET=/TOKEN=/PASSWORD=/API_KEY= assignment (pre-existing assertion, still passing), and the image is documented (docs/install-oci.md) to require any runtime secret to come from the operator's own container/orchestration secret mechanism. Bound to a real release, not an arbitrary claim: generate-oci-release.mjs refuses to run unless an evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json produced by MBR-903's own multi-platform-release.mjs already exists on disk with a matching self-consistent releaseId, and copies its tag/commit/release_generation verbatim into the OCI contract's identity -- proven by tests asserting both the happy path (identity fields match the fixture record) and the fail-closed path (no record present -> throws, no write).
gap: This task ships the binding script, its Containerfile fix, and deterministic tests; it does not itself produce a real image, SBOM, signature, or cosign receipt. Producing those still requires, on an operator's own Linux/server machine, entirely outside this task's hard rules (never run docker/podman/buildah/cosign/right-release/signing commands here): (1) a real MBR-903 release-generation.json for a tagged revision (which itself requires macOS/Windows signed builds per MBR-901/MBR-902's own acceptance gaps -- none exist yet, per those tasks' own evidence); (2) building the Linux `membrane` binary and the image itself with `podman build` / `docker build` against packaging/oci/Containerfile; (3) generating a real SBOM (e.g. syft), an Ed25519 signature, and a cosign receipt for that image; (4) running the built image rootless and capturing a real health/secret-scan receipt; (5) then running `node scripts/release/oci/generate-oci-release.mjs ... --write` with all of the above as real paths. Until then packaging/oci/release.v1.json correctly stays `state: "unavailable"`, and this image is not published, pulled, or promoted anywhere -- publication remains Adrian's decision, not this task's. Also declared, not new: release/contracts/platforms.v1.json has no `linux` target and this task does not add one (outside MBR-910's allowlist); the OCI image is bound to the same source identity as desktop builds via release-generation.json rather than via a RightKit-sealed platform target. Deferred to the Book 3 final phased gate, consistent with MBR-903's own acceptance.json gap note.
